description: SOC-thermal voltage model: V = OCV(SOC) - I*R(T), with Arrhenius resistance and capacity correction

cell.name: Standard NiCd D-cell (sintered plate)
cell.source: Berndt (2003), Maintenance-Free Batteries, Wiley; Shepherd (1965), J. Electrochem. Soc. 112, 657

R_ref.note: Internal resistance at T_ref; NiCd has very low R due to sintered plates

ocv_coefficients.description: OCV(SOC) = a0 + a1*SOC + a2*SOC^2 + a3*SOC^3 + a4*SOC^4 + a5*SOC^5
ocv_coefficients.source: Fitted to NiCd OCV discharge curve; relatively flat plateau at 1.2-1.25V (NiOOH/Ni(OH)2 couple)

E_a.note: Activation energy for NiCd; lower than Li-ion because aqueous electrolyte has higher conductivity with less T sensitivity
E_a.source: Berndt (2003), Maintenance-Free Batteries; Plett (2015), Battery Management Systems Vol.2

alpha_c.note: NiCd capacity temperature coefficient; moderate compared to Li-ion

dOCV_dT.note: NiCd entropic coefficient dOCV/dT ~ -0.60 mV/K; among the most negative for aqueous battery systems. The NiOOH + H2O + e- -> Ni(OH)2 + OH- reaction has large negative entropy. This makes NiCd warm significantly during discharge.
dOCV_dT.source: Berndt (2003), Maintenance-Free Batteries, Wiley; Thomas & Newman (2003), J. Electrochem. Soc. 150, A176

current.note: Negative=charge, Positive=discharge; NiCd tolerates very high rates

temperature.note: -30 to 60 degC; NiCd has excellent low-T performance
